pages:
A LEGEND OF
AURELITH
for travellers who
arrive by gate or
by water.

Corvin, harbour-
master, Vesper
Quays. C. 1102.

THE GATES
Four towers, four
beams. From the
plain, walk toward
the light: every
beam stands on a
gate. Soprano N,
Alto E, Tenor S,
Bass W.

THE PLAZA OF THE
HELD NOTE
At the centre. The
Heart hangs above
its dais. Canticle
Way runs north and
south from here,
Held Note Avenue
east and west.

Mind the Podium,
facing the Heart.
It is the
conductor's. Do not
stand on it. People
do. The Wardens
have views.

THE VESPER QUAYS
Follow the glow.
The river crosses
the city under
three arched
bridges. Moor at
the stone posts,
not the lamps.

THE ARCADE OF
ECHOES
The long market
under the columns.
Everything is paid
for in echoes.
Hesper's lamps are
fair; others less.

THE STILLHOUSES
The quiet quarter.
Terraces, dark
glass, amber eaves.
If a door is shut,
they are sleeping.
If it is open,
knock anyway.

THE ARCHIVE OF
ECHOES
The tower of
shelves. Listen
first; the
Listeners will
not let you in
otherwise.

STARWARD
The domed tower.
Climb it on a
strong aurora.

THE QUIET GARDENS
Stepped terraces.
No talking. Truly.

THE CONDUCTOR'S
SPIRE
The tallest tower.
From its top
terrace the four
beams, the river
and the Heart all
line up. Go once.
Everyone should.

THE FOUR VOICES

The Chord is four
parts sung as one.
Aurelith has a
gate for each, and
each gate a light
that stands into
the sky.

SOPRANO, north.
The high voice
keeps watch. Its
beam is the palest.
The Last
Procession left
the city by it.

ALTO, east.
The warm voice
welcomes. Most
travellers come in
under its beam, and
the Arcade opens
to meet them.

TENOR, south.
The bright voice
carries. Its beam
reaches furthest;
the lighthouses on
the plains were
tuned from it.

BASS, west.
The deep voice
holds. Its beam is
the darkest and the
steadiest. In every
chord the bass is
the floor the
others stand on.

Four statues face
the Heart, one for
each voice. Their
faces are blank so
anyone may sing in
them.

A chord is raised
as a house is: the
floor first, the
roof last. Deep,
bright, warm, high.
Sung any other way
it falls.

The Alto keeps the
lamplighters' song:
the hearth, the
river, the Chord,
the hearth again.
The Hall's cabinet
was tuned to it.

The fourth voice
points down.
It always has.
